body: This particular note may be incorrect as per https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/105051/files#r2035580642 (only in 2D, not 3D).

I copied this motion related block from `rest_info`, but I don't really know what's the purpose of this. According to the 
`get_rest_info` doc (the 3D one at least), motion should not affect the results.
Not sure why this check is needed. Jolt shouldn't return hits further away than the max penetration distance.
Don't you want the closest points instead (`JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti`)?

Optimization opportunity: Fetching `p_result_max` hits here and then generating the manifold in the for loop below means you can get up to `4 * p_result_max`. Better would be to create a collector that directly generates the manifold so that you can early out as soon as you've found `p_result_max` points and there are no hits with deeper penetration anymore.
This continue doesn't make sense at the end of the loop
How do I know in the collector (AddHit) that there won't be hits with deeper penetration anymore? Don't I need to get all hits to determine the deepest ones?

The collector implements `UpdateEarlyOutFraction` which you can populate with the value returned by `GetEarlyOutFraction` on the collision result. Jolt will stop calling the collector's `AddHit` function if it sees that there are no deeper hits anymore.

See for example: https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/blob/f8a329a6406d961349bc86dc477512e55358cebe/Jolt/Physics/Collision/CollisionCollectorImpl.h#L66-L78

Would the same optimization apply here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/15a4311583fbaad2eee5d2ecda5437eb9fd68c63/modules/jolt_physics/spaces/jolt_physics_direct_space_state_3d.cpp#L318C1-L388C3 ?
IIRC this is for collecting `p_max_collisions` number of the deepest collision points at the end position of `body_test_motion`. (This is where I copied the code from.) If so, then maybe it would be better to optimize `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti` with your suggestion first, rather than to create a new collector here.

The code you're pointing at has problems. See discussion at: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/114605#issuecomment-3764040803. That post contains a [link](https://github.com/jrouwe/godot/tree/114605) to an example on how you could extend `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti` to add additional logic that you need here. I don't think there's anything wrong with `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti`, you just want additional behavior (i.e. run the manifold calculations and pass the hits on to the base collector).

I ended up extending `CollideShapeCollector` instead of `JoltQueryCollectorClosestMulti`, because I couldn't figure out how to map the calculated contact points to the `hits` array of the base collector, without doing the same insertion sorting the base collector already does. Now i just store each hit and its calculated points together in a `struct`, and sort those. Is this wrong?

As far as I can see, your array of `hits_with_contact_points` is in order of early out fraction. If you take the first hit's early out fraction then you will never find anything that's further away than that hit anymore. I think you need to take the last element of the array instead.

This looks incorrect. What you probably wanted to do is iterate over `hits_with_contact_points` and over `contact_points`, summing up the number of entries and discarding all entries after you've counted to `max_points`. Since each `hit_with_contact_points` entry can contain up to 4 hits, it's likely that the total size of `hit_with_contact_points` is not going to reach `max_points`.
